transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The U.S. Supreme Court formally opens a new term today.
Their docket is jam-packed with controversies.
Among the big cases so far are legal tests of religious rights and bans on semi-automatic
weapons.
There's much more, as NPR's Nina Totenberg tells us.
The opening case before the justices tests whether state and local governments can sue
energy companies for allegedly deceiving the public about the damaging effects of fossil
fuels.
Also on the docket is another Colorado case that centers on a state law that provides
funding for a universal preschool program that's open to all students regardless of
race, religion, sexual orientation, or gender identity.
A Catholic parish is challenging the program's anti-discrimination provision, contending
that it violates its free exercise of religion.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
Tennessee's Governor Bill Lee says the head of Tennessee's prison system is resigning.
That is after last week's failed execution of Christa Pike.
The governor also says that former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton will lead an investigation into
what happened during the execution.
From member station WPLN in Nashville, Mariana Bacaiau has more.
Lee called for the third party review after last week's botched execution left Christa
Pike in critical condition but alive at a local hospital.
The current lethal injection process was developed after Stanton's last review found problems
with how the state inspected the drugs it uses to carry out the death penalty.
Lee says Stanton's investigation will determine if the current protocol was followed and evaluate
its effectiveness from there.
In the meantime, the governor has called off the remaining executions scheduled for this
year.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacaiau in Nashville.
The British Navy says five oil tankers were struck in major waterways in the Mideast over
the weekend.
Commercial ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted since the U.S. and Israel
began attacking Iran more than seven months ago.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reports.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center, which is run by the British Navy,
said a crew was safe and an investigation was underway after a commercial tanker reported
explosions near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Bab al-Mandab is an alternate waterway on the Red Sea used to transport oil.
Saudi ships have been targeted there by the Iranian-backed Yemeni Houthi rebels.
In separate incidents, four tankers were struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday
and Sunday, according to the British organization.
One vessel suffered damage to its engine room.
It was unclear who launched those attacks.
Oil has been flowing more steadily in recent weeks as the U.S. military, which maintains
a blockade of Iranian ports, guides vessels across the Strait.
It has yet to recover its pre-war mark.
Hadil Al-Shelchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
This is NPR.
President Trump is going to campaign in Nebraska today with Republican Senator Pete Ricketts.
The incumbent GOP senator is facing a strong challenge from independent candidate Dan Osborne.
He is supported by national Democrats.
Trump has been facing criticism from U.S. ranchers, including those in Nebraska, to
allow beef imports.
These beef imports will compete with U.S. ranchers.
Huge new data centers have many people wondering who pays for the upgrades to the electrical
grid needed to power those facilities.
NPR Scott Newman says the answer is not an easy one.
Connor Waldock is chief strategy officer at Grid Status, a company that focuses on providing
electricity market data.
He says the costs to upgrade the grid for AI are being shouldered by everyone who buys
electricity.
We're talking tens to hundreds of millions of dollars that are being built by these local
utilities that in many cases are just ultimately going to end up in customers' bills.
He says no one has quite figured out the fairest way to divvy up those costs.
In 2024, Maryland forecast that the cost of AI would add as much as $216 a year to the
average customer's bill.
Scott Newman, NPR News.
This year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine goes to three scientists, Karl Deistert, Peter
Hegeman and Georg Nagel.
They've researched ways to study the brain.
The Nobel Committee says they looked at ways to switch on or off the activity of individual
nerve cells in a living brain.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
In a war zone, reporting is a deadly gamble where you have to balance risk and reward.
For one Fox News reporter, that calculation ended in tragedy.
The whole person would have been injured if Benjy had just listened to the advisory.
Who's responsible for setting limits on reporting in a war zone when lives are on the line?
Listen now to the Sunday Story from the Up First podcast on the NPR app.
